content: The interaction between citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and sofosbuvir/velpatasvir can reduce the effectiveness of the latter by increasing gastric pH, which decreases velpatasvir solubility (it becomes practically insoluble at pH > 5). This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. To mitigate this, separate the administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir and antacids by at least 4 hours, and monitor the patient closely. Clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting the metabolism of CYP3A4 enzymes. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Similarly, clobazam decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Velpatasvir is metabolized by CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4 enzymes. Drugs that are moderate-to-potent inducers of these enzymes can significantly reduce velpatasvir plasma concentrations, potentially diminishing its therapeutic effect. Avoid or use alternative drugs in such cases. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases colchicine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Avoid colchicine use with P-gp inhibitors, especially in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing guidelines. Conivaptan increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cyclophosphamide also increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels, but the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Dabrafenib decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Similarly, dexamethasone reduces sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels through the same mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dexlansoprazole and other proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) reduce sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by increasing gastric pH, which decreases velpatasvir solubility. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If medically necessary, administer sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with food 4 hours before omeprazole 20 mg. The use of other PPIs has not been studied. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases digoxin levels by inhibiting P-gp. Monitor digoxin levels closely and adjust the dose as needed. Refer to digoxin prescribing information for guidance on dose modifications. Dipyridamole levels may increase when coadministered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir's inhibition of the BCRP transporter. Monitor closely. Similarly, doxorubicin levels may increase for the same reason. Use caution and monitor closely. Drospirenone increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, but the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Efavirenz decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Elagolix decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. Elbasvir/grazoprevir levels may increase due to velpatasvir's inhibition of OATP transporters. Monitor closely. Eluxadoline levels may increase when coadministered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir's inhibition of OATP transporters. Monitor closely. Similarly, enalapril levels may increase for the same reason. Use caution and monitor closely. Enzalutamide decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Eslicarbazepine acetate also reduces sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels through the same mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Esomeprazole and other PPIs reduce sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If necessary, administer sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with food 4 hours before omeprazole 20 mg. Etravirine decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Everolimus levels may increase when coadministered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust the dose if needed. Ezetimibe levels may increase due to velpatasvir's inhibition of OATP transporters. Monitor closely. Famotidine and other H2 receptor antagonists reduce sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer H2 receptor antagonists simultaneously with or 12 hours apart from sofosbuvir/velpatasvir at doses not exceeding famotidine 40 mg BID. Fexofenadine levels may increase due to velpatasvir's inhibition of OATP transporters. Monitor closely. Fluvastatin levels may also increase for the same reason. Use caution and monitor closely. Fluvoxamine increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Fosphenytoin decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inducing P-gp and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
